## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

// Start gameplay once without guessing between multiple controls or following links.
export async function startForCapture(page, { enabled = true, selector = '', timeout = 3000 } = {}) {
  if (!enabled) return { clicked: false, reason: 'disabled' }
  const candidate = selector
    ? page.locator(selector)
    : page.locator('button, input[type="button"], input[type="submit"], [role="button"]')
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeout
  do {
    const matches = []
    for (const control of await candidate.all()) {
      if (!await control.isVisible() || !await control.isEnabled()) continue
      const eligible = await control.evaluate((element, explicit) => {
        if (element.closest('a[href], form') || element.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true') return false
        if (explicit) return true
        const label = element.getAttribute('aria-label') || element.value || element.textContent || ''
        return /^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i.test(label.trim())
      }, Boolean(selector))
      if (eligible) matches.push(control)
    }
    if (matches.length > 1) return { clicked: false, reason: 'ambiguous' }
    if (matches.length === 1) {
      try { await matches[0].click({ trial: true, timeout: 2000 }) }
      catch (error) {
        if (error.name === 'TimeoutError') return { clicked: false, reason: 'not-actionable' }
        throw error
      }
      await matches[0].click({ timeout: 2000, noWaitAfter: true })
      return { clicked: true }
    }
    if (Date.now() >= deadline) break
    await page.waitForTimeout(Math.min(200, Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now())))
  } while (Date.now() <= deadline)
  return { clicked: false, reason: 'not-found' }
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a browser horror game where the player crashes a car in a forest, finds 20 scattered car pieces while a giant creepy wolf stalks/jumpscares them, and make it work on mobile.

## Requirements
- "Make a horror game about u ina forest and u need to drive around but a Giant Creeepy wolf made u crash and Now u need to find the scattered 20 Car pices Around the map while the giant Wolf 🐺 Goes after u Stalks u Junpscares u *the jumpscare is gunna be very scary) and Stalks u"
- "And make sure the game is fittable for mobile" — responsive layout, touch controls, safe areas, playable portrait/landscape.

## Decisions
- Single-page static HTML/JS with self-hosted Three.js (r0.160.0) and self-hosted fonts; no framework/build step (works with default start script).
- Procedural everything: forest, terrain, road, crashed car, 20 car parts, wolf model, and synthesized WebAudio (no external assets).
- Narrative flow: title screen → auto-driving intro (headlights, wolf in road) → crash → wake beside wreck → collect 20 parts → return to car → final scare ending.
- Desktop: pointer-lock FPS controls, WASD, Shift sprint, Ctrl crouch, F torch, Q sense, Esc pause. Mobile: virtual stick, drag look, RUN/TORCH/SENSE buttons.
- Wolf AI states: `lurk`, `prowl`, `hunt`, `retreat`, `caught`; torch beam slows it, sprinting provokes it, deaths keep collected pieces.
- Jumpscare rebuilt as a dedicated full-screen Three.js scare scene/face shot instead of a camera-attached head (previous version clipped into the camera and was unreadable).

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css` with title, how-to, HUD, pause, death, ending screens, cinematic caption, mobile controls, film grain/vignette.
- `src/util.js` noise, geometry merge, procedural glow/beam/smoke textures.
- `src/audio.js` procedural ambience, heartbeat, growls, howls, steps, pickup, crash, jumpscare, engine loop.
- `src/world.js` foggy night forest, moon/clouds/stars, terrain, winding road, ~600 instanced pines, undergrowth, 20 car parts with beams/glows, detailed crashed car, beacon, pickup bursts.
- `src/wolf.js` giant wolf model, animation/AI, and new `Jumpscare` class with its own scene/camera/lights.
- `src/player.js` FPS movement, collision, stamina/battery, torch spotlight, held torch model.
- `src/main.js` game state machine, intro drive, wake, HUD, pickups, sense compass, death/retry, repair/ending, pause, touch controls, render loop (renders scare scene when active).
- Verified in Chromium: title, intro, crash/wake, play, pickup, HUD, mobile reach `play` mode with touch controls visible. No page errors.

### Active
- Tuning the new full-screen jumpscare: latest screenshot `screenshots/j-early.png` shows a poorly framed close-up (giant black nose/skull, eye glows behind), not yet a readable scary wolf face. Needs camera/position/scale fixes.
- The test reported `jumpscare.active false, mode dead` quickly; likely low SwiftShader FPS + time-skip logic, but verify timeline/render before concluding.
- Overall art polish: stylized low-poly trees are still flat/Christmas-tree-like; held torch may still be oversized; intro cockpit framing/wolf reveal could improve.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Fix `Jumpscare` framing in `src/wolf.js`: move camera farther back / raise it, reduce head scale or snout length for scare variant, aim camera at face center, ensure eyes + open mouth + teeth read clearly; re-test with `jumpscare.t` set manually.
2. Confirm jumpscare renders instead of main scene and transitions `scare → dead` correctly; reduce reliance on dt during tests.
3. Re-check mobile portrait + landscape screenshots (`screenshots/m2-title.png`, `m2-play.png`), safe areas, no control/HUD overlap.
4. Test full gameplay loop: collect multiple parts, sense compass, wolf chase/audio, retry, 20th part → return to wreck → repair → ending screen.
5. Polish visuals/perf if time: tree silhouettes, flashlight, wreck readability.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game states, intro/wake, HUD wiring, render loop, all event handling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/wolf.js`: wolf model/AI and `Jumpscare` class (current focus).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: world, wreck, forest, 20 parts, atmosphere.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: movement/camera/torch/touch values.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: synthesized horror audio + engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/util.js`: noise/geometry/texture helpers used everywhere.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: screens, HUD, cinematic caption, import map.

## Objective
- Build a browser horror game where the player crashes a car in a forest, finds 20 scattered car pieces while a giant creepy wolf stalks/jumpscares them, and make it work on mobile.

## Requirements
- "Make a horror game about u ina forest and u need to drive around but a Giant Creeepy wolf made u crash and Now u need to find the scattered 20 Car pices Around the map while the giant Wolf 🐺 Goes after u Stalks u Junpscares u *the jumpscare is gunna be very scary) and Stalks u"
- "And make sure the game is fittable for mobile" — responsive layout, touch controls, safe areas, playable portrait/landscape.

## Decisions
- Single-page static HTML/JS with self-hosted Three.js (r0.160.0) and self-hosted fonts; no framework/build step.
- Procedural everything: forest, terrain, road, crashed car, 20 car parts, wolf model, and synthesized WebAudio (no external assets).
- Narrative flow: title → auto-driving intro (headlights, wolf in road) → crash → wake beside wreck → collect 20 parts → return to car → final scare ending.
- Desktop: pointer-lock FPS controls, WASD, Shift sprint, Ctrl crouch, F torch, Q sense, Esc pause. Mobile: virtual stick, drag look, RUN/TORCH/SENSE buttons.
- Wolf AI states: `lurk`, `prowl`, `hunt`, `retreat`, `caught`; torch beam slows it, sprinting provokes it, deaths keep collected pieces.
- Jumpscare is a dedicated full-screen Three.js scene/face shot with its own `buildScareHead()` model, not a camera-attached body head.
- Scare camera adapts to portrait: `camera.position.z = 12.2` when aspect < 0.85, otherwise 9.0; head yaw base 0.03 portrait / 0.09 desktop.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css` with title, how-to, HUD, pause, death, ending screens, cinematic caption, mobile controls, film grain/vignette.
- `src/util.js` noise, geometry merge, procedural glow/beam/smoke textures.
- `src/audio.js` procedural ambience, heartbeat, growls, howls, steps, pickup, crash, jumpscare, engine loop.
- `src/world.js` foggy night forest, moon/clouds/stars, terrain, winding road, ~600 instanced pines, undergrowth, leaf litter/twigs/logs, 20 car parts with beams/glows, detailed crashed car, beacon, pickup bursts.
- `src/wolf.js` giant wolf model/AI plus `buildScareHead()` and rebuilt `Jumpscare` with amber slit eyes, shortened snout, open tooth-lined mouth, rounded tongue, portrait-aware framing.
- `src/player.js` FPS movement, collision, stamina/battery, torch spotlight, smaller held torch with mobile scale (0.62 portrait / 0.9 desktop).
- `src/main.js` game state machine, intro drive, wake, HUD, pickups, sense compass, death/retry, repair/ending, pause, touch controls, render loop; HUD auto-hides during full scares.
- Verified desktop: title, intro cockpit/wolf reveal, crash/wake, play, pickup, HUD, sense compass, 20/20 collection, repair orbit with wolf reveal, ending screen, death screen, retry preserving pieces. No page errors.
- Verified mobile portrait 390×844 and landscape 844×390: title/play/sense/scare screenshots, touch controls visible, no HUD overlaps after layout fix, portrait scare properly framed.
- Fixed real bugs: `retry()` referenced non-existent `#danger`; `#compass-label` missing id caused per-frame `textContent` errors; HUD showed during full jumpscare; mobile meters overlapped stick/subtitle; desktop key hints showed on touch landscape.
- Intro cockpit polished: thinner A-pillars, slimmer roof/header, brighter raised amber gauges and radio, headlights moved ahead of hood (z -4.35) so the bonnet stays dark.

### Active
- Final visual polish/readability: current intro cockpit gauges/radio are large and flat; t-intro-wolf framing works but cockpit art may still be improved.
- Scare head reads clearly but remains stylized/cartoonish; could refine brow/eyes/fur further if desired.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Review latest intro screenshots (`screenshots/t-intro-idle.png`, `t-intro-wolf.png`) and optionally reduce gauge/radio scale or add windshield detail.
2. Re-run `/tmp/opencode/test-jump.cjs` and inspect `js-hold.png` after tongue/yaw changes; confirm the scare still reads on desktop and portrait.
3. Run a final regression pass: `/tmp/opencode/test-game.cjs`, `/tmp/opencode/test-e2e.cjs`, `/tmp/opencode/test-mobile.cjs`; confirm zero page errors and all state transitions.
4. Optionally improve forest tree silhouettes and overall atmosphere/performance.
5. Commit the uncommitted work when satisfied.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game states, intro/wake, HUD wiring, render loop, event handling, repair/ending, scare HUD hiding.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/wolf.js`: wolf model/AI, `buildScareHead()`, `Jumpscare` class and portrait camera adaptation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: world, wreck, forest, 20 parts, atmosphere.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: movement/camera/torch/touch and held-torch sizing.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: synthesized horror audio + engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/util.js`: noise/geometry/texture helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: screens, HUD, cinematic caption, import map, `#compass-label`.

# THE HOLLOW — 20 Pieces

A first-person browser horror game. You crash on a forest road, wake beside the wreck,
and have to recover twenty scattered car parts while something very tall follows you
between the trees.

Everything is procedural — forest, road, wreck, wolf, and audio. There are no external
assets or network requests, and no build step.

## Run

ES modules need to be served over HTTP:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
# then open http://localhost:3002
```

## Controls

| Desktop | |
| --- | --- |
| WASD / arrows | Walk |
| Shift | Sprint (uses stamina) |
| Ctrl | Crouch (quiet) |
| F | Torch (uses battery) |
| Q | Sense the nearest part |
| Esc | Pause |

On touch devices a virtual stick, drag-to-look, and RUN / TORCH / SENSE buttons appear
automatically. Layouts adapt to portrait and landscape and respect safe-area insets.

## Rules

- Find all 20 parts, then return to the wreck to repair the car.
- Sprinting, torchlight, and staring draw the wolf in. It can be slowed by the beam.
- When it catches you, you keep the parts you have already found and wake up back at the car.

## Structure

- `index.html` — screens, HUD, mobile controls
- `styles.css` — interface, responsive and safe-area rules
- `src/main.js` — state machine, intro, pickups, repair, endings, input
- `src/world.js` — terrain, road, forest, wreck, parts
- `src/wolf.js` — wolf model and AI, close-up jumpscare
- `src/player.js` — movement, camera, torch, touch
- `src/audio.js` — synthesized ambience and effects
- `src/util.js` — noise, geometry, texture helpers
- `vendor/three.module.js` — vendored Three.js r160
- `assets/fonts/` — self-hosted fonts
